name: biosig
desc: Tools for biomedical signal processing and data conversion
why: Biomedical signal conversion tools for EEG and ECG formats; real science, but the niche is narrow and the tools are file converters.

brief.what_it_is: BioSig is an open source software library for biomedical signal processing, covering biosignals such as EEG, ECoG, ECG, EOG, EMG and respiration. The homepage describes it as several parts: a toolbox for Octave and Matlab with data import/export filters, feature extraction, classification and a viewing and scoring tool; a C/C++ library with reading and writing routines for many biosignal data formats; rtsBCI, a real-time BCI system in Matlab and Simulink; and BioProFeed and BCIx, which the homepage lists without description. The executables you scouted (bin2rec, biosig2gdf, save2gdf, save2scp and others) are not named on the pages I read, so I could not confirm their individual functions. The data-conversion angle is real, but the homepage presents BioSig as a much broader signal-processing toolkit.
brief.why_it_exists: The aim of the BioSig project is to foster research in biomedical signal processing by providing open source software tools for many different applications. The homepage says the field needs solutions for data acquisition, artifact processing, quality control, feature extraction, classification, modeling and visualization, and that BioSig tries to cover them.

brief.install_notes: Download page (fetched from a guessed path, linked from the homepage nav) lists v3.9.8 for source, Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, ArchLinux, Cygwin and Win32/Win64 binaries, and a Homebrew route via the schloegl/biosig tap. Octave installs from a source tarball with pkg install. The Python package needs libbiosig installed first. Matlab users get mexbiosig and an EEGLAB plugin set (v3.8.5). No accounts or hardware needed for the libraries that I saw. I did not see the build steps for the executables themselves.
brief.standout: BioSig covers many biosignal formats through one library and is free under GPL, with bindings across Octave, Matlab, C/C++, Python, Java, R and Mathematica. Its file-format converters are part of a much wider research toolkit that also includes a real-time BCI system and a viewer.
brief.status: Probably maintained. The download page lists the same current version, v3.9.8, across source, binaries, Python, Java, R and Mathematica, and it mentions Python 3.14 support. I did not see a release date or last-commit date on either page, so I cannot confirm how recent it is.
brief.caveats: The homepage has no install commands of its own; it sends you to the Download and Documentation pages. Some components are older than the core (Octave v3.9.5, Matlab plugins v3.8.5, Mathematica v2.4.3 and v3.9.0). I did not see the executables' usage text or any man-page material. The Python package needs a separately installed libbiosig. The broad description on the homepage does not match the narrow file-converter framing in the scout notes. The Homebrew formula name 'biosig' comes from the download page. brew_caveats was empty.
quotes: BioSig is an open source software library for biomedical signal processing, featuring for example the analysis of biosignals such as the electroencephalogram (EEG), electrocorticogram (ECoG), electrocardiogram (ECG), electrooculogram (EOG), electromyogram (EMG), respiration, and so on.
The aim of the BioSig project is to foster research in biomedical signal processing by providing open source software tools for many different applications.
Everything in this project is freely available under the GNU General Public License.
